drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find our initial revisions for discussion. We propose six months of base-salary severance for a termination without Cause, subject to a release, and have clarified the scope of the restrictive covenant. Compensation remains open for agreement. Please provide the Executive's compensation proposal and any comments on these terms.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual Base Salary in an amount to be mutually agreed in writing and incorporated into this Agreement before execution, payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices and subject to required withholding. The Executive may participate in employee benefit plans generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to their terms. Any bonus or equity award must be separately approved and documented in writing.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause, the Company shall pay all accrued salary and other amounts required by applicable law. In addition, subject to the Executive executing and not revoking a customary release of claims within 60 days following termination, the Company shall pay severance equal to six months of the Executive's then-current Base Salary, excluding bonuses, equity and benefits. Severance shall be paid in substantially equal installments over six months under the Company's regular payroll practices, beginning on the first payroll date after the release becomes effective, subject to applicable tax requirements. If the release period spans two calendar years, payments shall commence in the second year, with any delayed installments paid on the first payment date. 'Cause' means fraud, embezzlement, conviction of or a plea of guilty or no contest to a felony involving dishonesty, willful misconduct causing material harm to the Company, or material breach of this Agreement or persistent failure to perform material duties. For a curable breach or failure to perform, Cause requires written notice describing the deficiency and failure to cure within 30 days. No severance is payable on resignation or termination for Cause.

4. NON-COMPETE. To the extent permitted by applicable law, for twelve months following termination of employment, the Executive shall not perform duties substantially similar to those performed for the Company for a business directly competing with a Company business in which the Executive had material responsibility during the final twelve months of employment, within territories in which the Executive had material responsibility and the Company actively conducted that business. Passive ownership of less than two percent of a publicly traded company's outstanding securities shall not violate this provision. This restriction shall not apply where prohibited by applicable law.

Please delete the non-compete or, alternatively, limit it to six months, applicable only while the Company pays severance, and narrow Cause to exclude good-faith performance shortcomings.

drafter.private_reasoning: Propose a measured Company counteroffer: $425,000 salary, a performance-based 40% target bonus, and no binding equity commitment without separate approval and documentation. Retain six months of severance, but extend eligibility to narrowly defined Good Reason and provide limited health-premium support. Accept a six-month non-compete tied to severance payments and exclude good-faith performance shortcomings from Cause. These proposals remain subject to partner and client approval; no confidential negotiating authority is disclosed.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you for your proposal. Subject to client approval, the Company proposes a $425,000 Base Salary and a 40% target annual bonus tied to performance goals. Any equity award would require separate approval and definitive documentation before execution. We have retained six months of severance, while adding a defined Good Reason trigger and health-premium support for that period. To address your restrictive-covenant concerns, we have reduced the non-compete to six months and limited it to periods for which the Company pays severance. We have also excluded good-faith performance shortcomings from Cause. We hope these changes provide a workable basis for finalizing the agreement.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual Base Salary of $425,000, payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices and subject to required withholding. The Executive shall be eligible for an annual cash bonus with a target equal to 40% of Base Salary earned during the applicable year, with actual payment dependent on achievement of Company and individual performance goals established annually by the Board or its compensation committee. Any bonus shall be determined in good faith and paid no later than March 15 of the following year, subject to the Executive remaining employed through the applicable performance year-end, except as otherwise required by law. The Executive may participate in employee benefit plans generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to their terms. Any equity award requires separate Board or compensation committee approval and definitive written award documentation before execution of this Agreement; absent such approval and documentation, this Agreement provides no entitlement to an equity award.

3. SEVERANCE. Upon any termination of employment, the Company shall pay all accrued salary and other amounts required by applicable law. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, subject to the Executive executing and not revoking a customary release of claims within 60 days following termination, the Company shall also pay severance equal to six months of the Executive's then-current Base Salary, excluding bonuses, equity and benefits. If termination follows a reduction in Base Salary constituting Good Reason, severance shall be calculated using the Base Salary immediately preceding that reduction. Severance shall be paid in substantially equal installments over six months under the Company's regular payroll practices, beginning on the first payroll date after the release becomes effective, with any delayed installments paid on that date, subject to applicable tax requirements. If the release period spans two calendar years, payments shall commence in the second year. Subject to the same release requirement and the Executive's timely election of available continuation coverage, the Company shall reimburse the portion of the Executive's continuation health-coverage premiums exceeding the active-employee contribution for equivalent coverage, for up to six months following termination, ending earlier upon eligibility for coverage with a new employer. The Executive shall promptly notify the Company of such eligibility. 'Cause' means fraud, embezzlement, conviction of or a plea of guilty or no contest to a felony involving dishonesty, willful misconduct causing material harm to the Company, material breach of this Agreement, or willful and continued refusal to perform lawful material duties. For any curable conduct, Cause requires written notice describing the deficiency and failure to cure within 30 days. Good-faith errors of judgment, failure to achieve performance targets, and good-faith performance shortcomings shall not constitute Cause. 'Good Reason' means, without the Executive's written consent, a material reduction in Base Salary or target bonus opportunity, a material diminution of duties or authority, or a required relocation of the Executive's principal work location by more than 50 miles that materially increases the Executive's commute. Good Reason requires written notice specifying the condition within 30 days after the Executive becomes aware of it, failure by the Company to cure within 30 days after receipt of notice, and resignation within 30 days after the cure period expires. No severance is payable upon resignation without Good Reason or termination for Cause.

4. NON-COMPETE. To the extent permitted by applicable law, for six months following termination of employment, and only for periods covered by Base Salary severance payments under Section 3 that the Company timely pays in accordance with that section, the Executive shall not perform duties substantially similar to those performed for the Company for a business directly competing with a Company business in which the Executive had material responsibility during the final twelve months of employment, within territories in which the Executive had material responsibility and the Company actively conducted that business. Any initial payment delay expressly permitted under Section 3 shall not shorten the restriction if the Company timely pays the corresponding delayed installments. This restriction shall not apply following a termination for which no severance is payable under Section 3 and shall cease if the Company fails to make a severance payment when due. Passive ownership of less than two percent of a publicly traded company's outstanding securities shall not violate this provision. This restriction shall not apply where prohibited by applicable law.

receiver.message_back: Subject to our client’s approval, we can accept the $425,000 salary and 40% target bonus if severance and health-premium support increase to 12 months, severance includes the target bonus, and a without-Cause or Good Reason departure preserves any earned prior-year bonus and a prorated current-year bonus based on actual performance. We would retain the six-month, paid-only non-compete without extension, extend the Good Reason notice window to 90 days, and require any agreed equity grant to be approved and definitively documented before signing.
